after: ## What are the types of Tawhid and Shirk?
alt: Three aspects of tawhid: al-Rububiyyah (Allah alone is Lord), al-Uluhiyyah (Allah alone is worshipped) and al-Asma wa al-Sifat (His names and attributes are unique). Below, major shirk, such as worshipping idols, takes a person outside Islam; minor shirk, such as showing off in worship, damages the reward of good deeds.
caption: Three aspects of oneness, and two degrees of its opposite.

after: ## What are the key beliefs of Islam?
alt: Six beliefs on the left link to four effects on the right: belief in Allah gives purpose; revealed books and prophethood give guidance; angels and the Last Day give accountability; and Al-Qadr gives trust in Allah.
caption: Each belief does a job in a Muslim's life: purpose, guidance, accountability or trust.

after: ## What do the names of Allah teach?
alt: A table of five names: Qudrah, the All-Powerful, so Muslims rely on Him; Al-Khaliq, the Creator, so creation is a trust; Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim, the Most Gracious and Most Merciful, the names that open every sura but one; and Al-Alim, the All-Knowing, so Muslims act sincerely.
caption: Each name says something about Allah and something about how Muslims should live.

after: ## What are angels and what does the Hadith of Jibril teach?
alt: A stepped pyramid. The wide base is Islam, practice, the five pillars; above it is iman, belief in Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day and qadr; at the top is ihsan, excellence, worshipping Allah as though you see Him.
caption: Practice, belief and excellence: the three levels of faith Jibril taught.

alt: A sequence from death to Barzakh, resurrection and the Day of Judgement, splitting into Heaven for the righteous and Hell for the wicked. Below, the death rituals in order: ghusl, the kafan, the funeral prayer and burial facing the qibla, with their purposes.
caption: From death to judgement, and the rituals that honour the dead and remind the living.

after: ## What do the prophets and holy books teach?
alt: A table of prophets with a key point and their book: Adam, first human and prophet, taught repentance; Ibrahim, given the Suhuf; Musa, the Tawrat; Dawud, the Zabur; Isa, the Injil; and Muhammad (pbuh), the Seal of the Prophets, the Qur'an.
caption: Earlier books carried the same message; the Qur'an is final and the Prophet (pbuh) is the last.

after: ## How was the Muslim community led after the Prophet (pbuh)?
alt: A scaled timeline from 632 to 661: Abu Bakr (632–634) kept the community united and had the Qur'an gathered; Umar (634–644) expanded and organised the state; Uthman (644–656) distributed standard copies of the Qur'an; Ali (656–661) was known for knowledge and justice in a time of conflict. A note gives the Shi'a view of Ali as the first Imam.
caption: Four leaders in under thirty years, each remembered for a defining contribution.
